facts.text: I have been in dentistry for 13 years.
I do blood flow restriction (occlusion) training two days a week.
When I do blood flow restriction training, I get stronger within a couple weeks.
When I stopped blood flow restriction training for a while because my house was being remodeled and my exercise room was messed up, I lost some strength.
After restarting blood flow restriction training this week, I felt it again and noticed improvement.
I started using the product from the other person’s company and noticed better recovery within about a week.
I take a higher dose than the recommended dose because I put my body under strain.
I told a friend about the product and sent her a picture of it.
My friend said she had been taking the product for a long time and that it improves her workout.
I am a supplement snob and I do not take a lot of supplements.
I incorporated the other person’s product into my routine and was pleasantly surprised by it.
I have a relatively new product with electrolytes that I was told about, and it includes sodium and potassium, zinc, magnesium, trace elements, and two grams of Perfect Amino per scoop.
I have tried the electrolytes and I ran out of them.
I have a 60 hour work week.
I used to do between 20 and 22 hours per week of iron man training.
I usually take Mondays off.
On Saturdays, I warm up and then do a bike ride about five miles from where I am to the beach.
On Saturdays, I ride a junk heavy bike because it would get stolen if it were a nicer bike.
On Saturdays, there is a bridge with about a 3% grade for about a quarter mile on the route to the beach.
On Saturdays, after warming up I ride as hard as I can.
On Saturdays, I swim between 2,000 and 4,000 yards in open water.
On Saturdays, I run between 8 and 15 miles and then ride the bike back home easy.
On Sundays, I do a 40 to 90 mile ride depending on the day.
This Sunday, I will probably ride 70 or 75 miles because I am starting to ramp up.
On Tuesdays and Thursdays, I do a pool swim workout.
I am not doing masters pool swimming because the locker rooms are too crazy to use.
On Tuesdays and Thursdays, I also do an indoor bike interval workout on a trainer.
I have a Wahoo Kick and I want to get a Wahoo.
On Wednesdays and Fridays, I do interval runs.
My interval runs are usually three to six miles and include quarter miles, one-mile segments, and six to ten repeats.
My weekly training time is probably 10 to 12 hours per week.
I compete in an iron man age group with about 10 to 20 people.
I finished my first Ironman in 1982.
My first Ironman was Ironman Hawaii in 1982.
After finishing Ironman Hawaii in 1982, I could not remember why I wanted to do it and decided I was never going to do another one.
On the plane back after Ironman Hawaii in 1982, my training partner and I had the same feeling.
On the plane back after Ironman Hawaii in 1982, there were about 40 guys who had done their race.
By the time the plane landed after Ironman Hawaii in 1982, almost all of us decided to go back next year.
My philosophy is to keep doing it until you get it, and if you go down you get up and do it again.
